impact_radius.doc: impacts: spread of the points round each impact

impact_share.doc: impacts: share of the points placed at impacts (the rest are scattered everywhere)

merge_clusters.doc: Group the points into this many clusters (by distance, a k-means style pass) in the int point attribute 'cluster'; voronoi_fracture cluster_pieces merges their cells (0: -1 everywhere)

min_distance.doc: Keep points at least this far apart (0: off)

outgrp_clustered.doc: Points placed around a cluster centre

outgrp_clustered_name.doc: Name of the clustered points group

outgrp_extra.doc: Points that came in on the second input

outgrp_extra_name.doc: Name of the extra input points group

outgrp_impact.doc: impacts mode: points placed round an impact

outgrp_impact_name.doc: Name of the impact points group

outgrp_interior_name.doc: Name of the interior points group

outgrp_surface.doc: Points placed on the shape's surface

outgrp_surface_name.doc: Name of the surface points group

piece_attrib.doc: Point int attribute numbering the points (empty: none)

relax.doc: Lloyd relaxation passes on the interior points: pieces become more even in size

source.doc: impacts: the second input holds impact points (optional float 'impulse' = how hard); the fracture points gather round them

surface_fraction.doc: Share of the points placed on the surface instead of inside: more, smaller pieces at the outside, as in a shattering shell

outgrp_cutedges.doc: The edges that lie on a cut plane (the open border each cut left)

outgrp_cutedges_name.doc: Name of the cut edges group

outgrp_cutpoints.doc: The points that lie on a cut plane

outgrp_cutpoints_name.doc: Name of the cut points group

piece_attrib.doc: Primitive int attribute with each face's cell (the index of its point)

axis.doc: Axis along which the waves propagate.

frequency.doc: Spatial frequency of the sinusoidal waves.

offset.doc: Phase offset of the waves in radians.

strength.doc: Displacement amplitude along the surface normal.

group.doc: Only change these elements: group names, ^exclusions, numbers/ranges, or an expression like '@P.z > 0' (empty: all). Over vertices, a primitive group selects its corners

run_over.doc: Domain the snippet runs over: points, primitives (faces) or vertices (face corners)

snippet.doc: VEX-like expression run over every element, e.g. '@P.z += sin(@P.x * 2) * 0.5'. See the wrangle reference.
